Key points - There are seven strategies for moving an application to AWS: retire, retain, rehost, relocate, repurchase, replatform and refactor (re-architect). - Rehost (\"lift and shift\") moves an application unchanged. Replatform (\"lift, tinker and shift\") adds targeted optimisation, such as moving a database to a managed service, switching to Graviton processors, or containerising a virtual machine. - Relocate moves many servers at once to a cloud version of the same platform, such as VMware, without rewriting applications. - Repurchase replaces the application with a SaaS or newer product. Retire switches off applications with no remaining value; unused \"zombie\" applications (average CPU and memory below 5 percent) are typical candidates. - Retain leaves an application where it is, for example for data-residency rules, unresolved hardware dependencies, or mainframe and mid-range systems that need careful assessment first. - Refactor is the most complex and costly strategy. For large migrations the guidance is to rehost, replatform or relocate first and modernise after the move. Useful when: deciding what to do with each application in a customer's portfolio, and explaining why a full rewrite is rarely the first step.
